scope: Live checked compiler host product selection; not a semantic profile or live authority capability.

operations.emitArtifact: Executable and all metadata available from the selected compiler; present malformed requested metadata rejects this product request.
operations.emitExecutableArtifact: Executable and required IR evidence only; optional PublicApiIR/origin/erasure/generated-position products are not read or decoded.
operations.emitOriginGraph: Independent requested declaration origin product, with required PublicApiIR dependency.
operations.emitDeclarationsArtifact: Explicit direct-JS source declaration request under the session's fixed closed or uniform structural profile; returns executable and source declaration products from one staged emission, without requesting origin/generated-position products.
operations.emitSelectedArtifact: Explicit own boolean metadata/declarations/sourceMap flags; one staged emission serves their dependency closure. Declarations and required source maps are JavaScript products. sourceMap requires a complete available origin closure and fails if absent; metadata alone retains all-available semantics.

acceptance: Kernel acceptance uses the same frozen prepared Core and exact admissions, independently of optional origin-table shape.
A present malformed/failing origin-aware preparation API or missing/malformed prepared Core rejects without duplicate preparation or fallback.
Malformed origin-table data becomes an error only when origins are requested; accessors are not invoked.

Selected target-stage APIs execute once per emission. Failure, malformed required stage data, changed RuntimeIR/VerifiedIR bytes and failed specialization correspondence still reject executable-only output.
Selected stage fields must be own data properties. Unrequested metadata fields are neither read nor recursively frozen.
Source API projection and debug reconstruction are not invoked for executable-only output. Only selected returned products count against the output byte budget.
Revocation, session identity, CertifiedSource binding and target authorization apply to every selection.
Executable emission and source API projection recheck live session membership and exact admissions after invoking the selected producer and before returning its product.
specialization: Executable-only emission runs the existing independent exact-instantiation relation without allocating a debug witness map. Full metadata emission retains witnesses from the same relation.
compatibility: emitArtifact keeps its strict all-available-metadata behavior. No automatic fallback follows a requested-product failure. A caller explicitly requests executable-only output on its existing live handle.
limits: This host selection does not stop a selected portable staged producer from internally computing observation tables.
This is not a hostile-JavaScript sandbox or a resource theorem.
Exact Cargo/rustc dependency/toolchain capture, specialized-input migration, broader Canonical wrappers and broader named/dependent declaration types remain pending.

buildRouting.backend: Explicit typescript/javascript/wasm/rust; default typescript, never inferred from a file suffix.

products.typescript: metadata preserves the existing TS+tsc executable/declaration/source-map bundle; other product modes reject.
products.javascript: executable (default), metadata (all available metadata), declarations (portable source declarations), source-map (standalone JavaScript map), declaration-map (required source declarations and standalone declaration map with metadata), or all (declarations plus both map products). Explicit linked mode publishes separate sourceMappingURL-attached JavaScript and declaration identities, retaining original unlinked bytes in the archive.
products.wasm: executable (default) or metadata. Without --wasm-exports the existing private wasm32 self-host ABI is selected. With an explicit psc-wasm-canonical-selection/1 file, 32/64-bit source words and only its scalar exports are selected; interface/binding/policy products are required with the binary.
products.rust: source (default) or metadata emits .rs through the generated checked compiler or explicit products/3 native session and shared graph/archive/bundle publication. Current input is generic ValidatedRuntimeIR; no RustIR is invented. Source emission does not run Cargo/rustc or produce a native binary.

buildRouting.representation: --js-representation closed|uniform pins the live JavaScript profile before checking; other backends reject uniform.
buildRouting.compiler: An explicitly selected generated module must expose its selected staged API. The checked provider-specific default is retained; the CLI no longer injects an unrelated bootstrap compiler.
validation: Target/product/profile/suffix combinations reject before source/compiler loading; selected native direct sessions require the exact versioned protocol with no legacy fallback.
One live checked source session emits the selected direct products; session is closed after capture.
The graph compares all three requested declaration product identities and bytes with the live portable-comparison result.
Required source maps use generated-session live lineage or exact versioned native captured tables, then compose captured original-source preparation coordinates and output filename.
Only the TypeScript lane resolves or invokes tsc; direct lanes retain all graph/archive/descriptor/bundle/envelope checks.
Executable-only closed graphs check specialization correspondence without constructing a debug witness map.

Declaration maps use the same portable-compared declaration bytes and required captured source origins. A separate pass replays source-signature writer positions, composes original coordinates and publishes a versioned debug product; neither native transport tuple nor executable bytes change.
Linked selection requires both bound maps and exact filenames; new pass and archive replay independently reconstruct linked products.
buildRouting.publication: The existing single graph output inventory drives staged writes and per-file publication; receipt is last. No directory-atomic transaction or cleanup of pre-existing unselected files is claimed.
buildRouting.nativeTransport: Explicit psc-checked-seed-products/1 native transport supports direct JavaScript/wasm32 and selected products over one retained prepared source. Legacy TypeScript transport remains unchanged. Explicit products/3 supports Rust source/metadata with its Rust source representation contract and two frames; no legacy protocol fallback.
buildRouting.canonicalWasm: Generated and native products/2 sessions pin exact policy before checking and require the selected portable staged API. Shared independent interface projection and actual target/binary signature checks precede common graph/descriptor/bundle/envelope publication.
buildRouting.rustSource: The registry's executableArtifacts group includes role target-source. The evidence-envelope executableArtifact field binds its rust-source identity; it is not a native-executable acceptance claim. Receipt rustTarget.compilerInvoked and nativeBinaryProduced are false.
